Paper showing positive effect of Golden Rice on Vitamin A levels in children retracted. Though the retraction wasn't for any issues around the science (which was solid), but around the ethics.

Lead author of the study Guangwen Tang (of Tufts University) is accused of not gaining informed consent from parents of the children involved in the study and faking ethics approval documents.

On "informed consent":

[Tufts'] IRB should also have ensured that the informed consent form for parents explicitly stated that the rice is the product of genetic engineering.

U.S. guidelines stipulate that such forms use plain language understandable to lay people, and the IRB agreed to let Tang say that "Golden Rice is a new rice which makes beta-carotene," without using the loaded words "genetically modified." (The consent form for a very similar study by Tang among adults in Boston, published in 2009, didn't use that term either.) Given the sensitivities over transgenic food, which existed in China as well, that was the wrong decision, according to the external panel...

...Tufts has barred [Tang] from doing research on humans for 2 years, during which time she will be "retrained on human subjects research regulations and policies," the university stated; after the training is completed, for a further 2 years she can do human studies only as a supervised co-investigator.

Tang, 64, has decided to close her lab next year as a result of the punishment, says Adrian Dubock, executive secretary of the Golden Rice Humanitarian Board in Switzerland, which was not directly involved in the study. "She did not choose the political controversy thrust upon her altruistic research," Dubock, who has kept in contact with Tang, says in a written statement. ELI5: How do our bodies know we've had enough sleep and wake us up?

ELI5: Unlike the rest of our body, our brains allow waste material to build up and needs to flush them out once full. It forces us to "sleep" while these processes go on and wakes us up once the waste is completely cleaned out.

Expanded: Our bodies have multiple waste disposal systems to prevent the build up of toxins left over from feeding our cells (called the excretory system). From the neck down, these systems work constantly (waste travels back from our muscles into the liver, kidneys and so on). Our brains on the other hand do not do this (last i looked science is not sure why) and will build up waste material throughout the day. Our brains make us tired and when we fall asleep there are systems that turn on and flush out all the waste material at once. The more we use our brains during the day, the longer sleep we need because there is more waste to clean out. This is why learning something particularly challenging could make you want a nap right after. If you allow yourself to wake up naturally your brain is doing so the moment everything is clean and clear. If you get too little sleep, you have left over waste in your brain from the day before and will have trouble functioning mentally. For people who "catch up" on sleep over the weekend, you sleep longer because there is tons of waste. When we are young (from birth until our early 20s) we are using our brain a lot and we require more sleep. As we get older and our actions become more "muscle memory" we require less sleep.

Fun fact: if our brains had a constant waste disposal system like the rest of our body we wouldn't need to ever sleep.
